utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Unfortunately, Judge Van den Wyngaert, who was sitting yesterday in an appeal, has had to continue with the Appeal Chamber this morning. So we will sit under Rule 15 bis. We must go, I believe, into closed session now for the recall of Witness P002. So if we could close the court and recall the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. I think we decided to have the diary admitted into evidence, and the witness just took it away. If it stays with him, it won't be in evidence. I'm not sure if that's a problem or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood it was already in the custody of the court officer. If not, it will be recovered when we rise. But we will also make an order that at the conclusion of the trial, the diary be returned to the witness. We will have the photocopy which seems to have been of equal value as the original. And it will be, because of its personal significance to the witness, something that should be returned to him. He made this point when he was here last. That brings us now, Mr. Moore, to inquire whether you are in a position to indicate whether we are to have further evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back to open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, we will be making an application to call additional evidence. There is a matter that is being currently translated or interpreted. That is going to take five days, I checked that this morning, and then clearly, the Prosecution will make an application to call rebuttal evidence on that issue. Can I say there was -- there were two other areas that I was looking into. I don't -- and I mean no discourtesy in any way. In relation to one of them, I will not pursue that point; however, in relation to the other matter, I'm hoping to have a reply on that in the very near future. So the situation is I had hoped that there would be three topics or stroke witnesses. One almost certainly I will know within or three days. The second relates to matters that are being translated, and that will be known precisely -- the contents will be known precisely by the end of next week. However, it would not take a lengthy period of time for the evidence to be called and will easily fall within the time frame that the Court has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Moore. Clearly, notice needs to be given at the earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we have set aside Friday, the 12th of January to Wednesday the 16th, is it, maybe the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: 17th, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The mathematics of counsel are better than mine. Friday to Wednesday the 17th for the receiving of that additional evidence. And we need to keep within that time frame --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- because of other commitments. There are one or two matters still the subject of reserve decision by the Chamber, motions for the admission of certain documents. Those decisions will be delivered, I expect, in the course of the coming week so that all those matters should be clear and resolved. Are you standing with some other matter there, Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I regret to say I am. There is MFI 69, which is a translation. If I put it in ordinary terms, it was the Vance/Sljivancanin transcript. We had objected to various parts of that until the CLSS revision had been received. In our view, -- well, may I just clarify that in actual fact that it has now been received. Would Your Honour forgive me a moment. So that has not been received as yet and we are chasing that. There is another matter which is MFI 336. And as far as I'm aware, that has now been amended and a word has been added to the transcript, and we agreed to that. So MFI 336, we have no objection to that becoming an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There any objection to that, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was my proposal. We were just waiting for the transcript to arrive. The video has been admitted. This is the conversation between Pavkovic and Borsinger, and this was tendered and admitted when Mr. Kypr was here. This is Exhibit 335. 336 is the transcript that we had been waiting for to be agreed, and so we are on the same track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So MFI 133 the transcript will now be received in its amended form as Exhibit 133.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No, it's 336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript had it at 133.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think it's MFI, and the "I" looks like a 1. So I believe it's MFI 336. At least I believe it is the error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is now Exhibit 336. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as we told Mr. Moore yesterday, there are two other MFIs also in relation to Mr. Kypr. These documents were marked for identification when Mr. Kypr were here. These are two 1st Military District documents. I think Mr. Vasic were was the one that showed them. And they were just marked for identification at the time, but have not been made exhibits since. By your leave, Your Honours, by next Monday, we would be filing a motion with our arguments in relation to those two MFIs, 330 and 331. These are 1st Military District reports on the activities of the ECMM. I am sure you will remember. The same document of that kind was admitted, no objections from the OTP, but these two drew objections at the time. And for that reason, they were merely marked for identification at the time. The only oral submission that I can make right now based on my memory in terms of substance, in terms of form, these documents are identical to the document that was exhibited and drew no objection from Mr. Moore at the time. If that is all right, we are prepared to submit a written motion about this by next Monday, so the OTP can have a look and the trial can perhaps make a written ruling about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you are in a position to file on Monday, I would hope Mr. Moore will be in a position to respond by Wednesday so that we can decide by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I would have thought, with the utmost respect, the better approach would be if I can be shown the documents again, the reference to the transcript, and it may be it won't even require a motion. But if it does, then we will stick by the time table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a written note to say that counsel are agreed --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- would enable the document to be entered as an exhibit or the two documents. It's the spirit of agreement that is to be encouraged. Speaking of that, may the Chamber thank you all for your efforts and assistance this year and wish all of you the best for the festive season. And we will look forward to seeing you all in the new year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 12th day of January 2007

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
